description_summary: 12-month unduplicated enrollment headcounts broken down by student level and degree/certificate-seeking status, with undergraduate counts additionally split by full- or part-time attendance and, for degree/certificate-seeking students, first-time, transfer-in, and continuing status. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYALEV; columns include totals by sex and all nine race/ethnicity categories. The undergraduate attendance-status detail is available beginning with 2019–20 data, so it is available for 2020–21.

12-month unduplicated enrollment headcounts broken down by student level and distance-education status: exclusively distance education, some distance education, or no distance education. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYDLEV.

12-month instructional activity measured as total credit hours and/or contact hours delivered, broken down by undergraduate and graduate level. This table contains instructional-activity measures used to derive 12-month full-time-equivalent enrollment, not unduplicated student headcounts.

Institution-level academic library data for fiscal year 2021, covering library characteristics, collections, expenditures, services, and full-time-equivalent library staff. The survey applies only to degree-granting institutions; expenditure data are available only for institutions with total expenditures exceeding $100,000. Collection categories include physical and electronic serials, available since 2016–17.

Undergraduate admission considerations, applicant and admission counts, enrollment among admitted students, and SAT/ACT test-score data for entering first-time degree/certificate-seeking students. The table covers Fall 2021; it applies only to institutions without an open-admissions policy for entering first-time students, and SAT/ACT fields apply only where test scores are required for admission. Records are institution-level admissions data, with admission-consideration variables distinguishing whether each factor was required, considered but not required, or not considered; writing scores are not collected.

Awards and degrees conferred by 6-digit CIP program, award level, first or second major, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL; it contains total, men’s, and women’s awards, including the nine race/ethnicity categories. Beginning in 2019-20, less-than-one-year certificates are split into less than 12 weeks and at least 12 weeks but less than one year.

Students receiving any award or degree, broken out by race/ethnicity and gender. Each institution has one record uniquely identified by UNITID, with total recipients and men’s and women’s recipients for the nine race/ethnicity categories.

Students receiving awards or degrees, broken out by award level, race/ethnicity, gender, and age group. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and AWLEVEL; age categories are under 18, 18–24, 25–39, and 40 or older, but race, gender, and age cannot be cross-tabulated in combination. Beginning in 2019-20, less-than-one-year certificates are split into less than 12 weeks and at least 12 weeks but less than one year.

Programs offered and programs available entirely through distance education, broken out by CIPCODE and award level. Records are keyed by UNITID and CIPCODE and include six-digit program records with award-level indicators for programs offered, all programs available entirely by distance education, and some programs available entirely by distance education; two-digit CIP summaries count the six-digit programs in each group, and CIPCODE 99 provides institution totals. Beginning in 2019-20, less-than-one-year certificates are split into less than 12 weeks and at least 12 weeks but less than one year, and more detailed distance-education measures are available.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and attendance status and student level (EFLEVEL).

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), attendance status, and student level (EFALEVEL), with counts for all nine race/ethnicity categories.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by distance education status and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and student level (EFDELEV), and includes exclusive, some, and no distance education enrollment, with exclusive-distance counts further classified by student location.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), age category (EFBAGE), and student level (LSTUDY). Age-based enrollment reporting is optional in even-numbered years; 2021 (odd) has data.

First-time freshman counts broken down by state of residence, including counts who graduated from high school in the previous year. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and state of residence (EFCSTATE). Residence reporting is optional in odd-numbered years, so 2021 (odd) has data but participation is optional.

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio, identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID). The measures apply only to institutions with undergraduate students; entering-class data are reported only by academic-year institutions, and short-program institutions do not have retention data.

Fall enrollment counts in selected major fields—education, engineering, biological/life sciences, mathematics, physical sciences, business, law, dentistry, and medicine—broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), major field, attendance status, and student level (EFCIPLEV); the table covers four-year institutions only. Fall enrollment by major is not collected in odd-numbered years, so 2021 (odd) has no data.

Institution-level finance data for public institutions using GASB 34/35, with one row per UNITID, covering revenues, functional and natural-classification expenditures, endowments, assets, liabilities, and financial health measures. Beginning in fiscal year 2020, scholarship and fellowship amounts include discounts and allowances by source; detailed endowment data are available, while detailed functional expenditures and natural classifications for fringe benefits, operations and maintenance of plant, depreciation, and interest are unavailable beginning in fiscal year 2016.

Institution-level finance data for private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB, with one row per UNITID, covering revenues, functional and natural-classification expenditures, endowments, assets, liabilities, and financial health measures. Beginning in fiscal year 2020, scholarship and fellowship amounts include discounts and allowances by source; detailed endowment data are available, while detailed functional expenditures and natural classifications for fringe benefits, operations and maintenance of plant, depreciation, and interest are unavailable beginning in fiscal year 2016.

Institution-level finance data for private for-profit institutions using FASB, with one row per UNITID, covering revenues, functional and natural-classification expenditures, assets, liabilities, and financial health measures; this form does not provide the endowment detail included in the other finance forms. Beginning in fiscal year 2020, scholarship and fellowship amounts include discounts and allowances by source, and detailed functional expenditures and natural classifications for fringe benefits, operations and maintenance of plant, depreciation, and interest are unavailable beginning in fiscal year 2016.

Graduation-rate outcomes at 200% of normal time for full-time, first-time degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduates, using the 2013 cohort at four-year institutions and the 2017 cohort at less-than-4-year institutions. Institution-level records are organized by UNITID and graduation-status category (GRTYPE); four-year outcomes focus on bachelor’s degrees, while less-than-4-year outcomes cover any degree or certificate.

Fall graduation-rate outcomes for full-time, first-time degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduates, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity, with 150%-of-normal-time outcomes for four-year and two-year institutions. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID and GRTYPE; four-year records distinguish bachelor’s-degree seekers from other degree/certificate seekers, while two-year records use the 2018 cohort and four-year records use the 2015 cohort. The 100%-of-normal-time completion count is not available jointly by gender and race/ethnicity for two-year institutions.

Graduation-rate outcomes for the 2018 cohort of full-time, first-time degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduates at less-than-2-year institutions, including enrollment, completion within 100% or 150% of normal time, and transfer-out status. Institution-level records are defined by UNITID and graduation-status category (GRTYPE).

Graduation-rate outcomes at 150% of normal time, separated into three financial-aid subcohorts: Pell Grant recipients; subsidized Stafford Loan recipients who did not receive Pell; and students who received neither. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID and PSGRTYPE; four-year institutions use the 2015 bachelor’s and other-degree-seeking cohorts, while two-year and less-than-2-year institutions use the 2018 cohort.

Staff counts by full- or part-time status, medical-school status, occupational category, faculty status, tenure status, and non-tenure contract length. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPCAT, which defines the occupational and tenure-status category; multi-year and indefinite contract categories are available from 2016 onward.

Counts of full-time instructional staff by faculty/tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender, with non-tenure staff further divided by contract length. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID and SISCAT, which combines FACSTAT and ARANK; the table applies to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was mandatory in odd-numbered years and optional in even-numbered years beginning in 2001, and became mandatory annually in 2016, so 2021 (odd) has data.

Full-time new-hire counts by primary occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender, with instructional hires additionally classified by faculty/tenure status and, from 2016 onward, non-tenure contract length. New hires are permanent full-time hires made between November 1, 2020 and October 31, 2021; each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SNHCAT, which defines the occupation and instructional faculty/tenure category. The table applies to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices; race/ethnicity and gender reporting was mandatory in odd-numbered years and optional in even-numbered years beginning in 2001, and became mandatory annually in 2016, so 2021 (odd) has data.

Full- and part-time staff counts by occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender; each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and STAFFCAT, the occupational-category and full/part-time-status key. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was mandatory in odd-numbered years and optional in even-numbered years beginning in 2001, and became mandatory annually in 2016, so 2021 (odd) has data.

Counts of full-time instructional staff by academic rank, faculty status, tenure status, and non-tenure contract length. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID and FACSTAT, which combines faculty and tenure status; the table applies to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices.

Counts, salary outlays, average salaries, and equated 9-month salary measures for full-time, nonmedical instructional staff, broken out by academic rank, gender, and number of months worked. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK; staff working fewer than 9 months have counts but no salary data.
Counts and salary outlays for full-time, nonmedical, noninstructional staff, broken out by occupational category.

Custom comparison-group membership holds the submitting institution’s custom comparison group and its comparison institutions, including each comparison institution’s UNITID, name and state. The row grain is a submitting-institution/comparison-institution membership, with the comparison-group membership distinguishing entries when an institution submits more than one group.

Survey-component response and applicability statuses hold one institution-by-component record, keyed by UNITID and survey component. They distinguish responded, nonresponded/imputed, not-applicable, parent/child multi-campus reporting, and revised submissions in final or revised releases.

Directory information and institution-level classifications hold each institution’s name, address, contact and institutional URLs, active/Title IV status, control, level, highest offering and degree, and Carnegie classification. The row grain is one institution identified by UNITID.

Institution-level educational offerings, organization, admissions, services, athletic affiliations, control and special learning opportunities are keyed by UNITID. The fields include award-level offerings, open-admission status, distance-education offerings, library services and related organization or affiliation measures; beginning in 2020-21, less-than-one-year certificates are split into less-than-12-weeks and at-least-12-weeks-but-less-than-one-year categories.

Full-academic-year student charges are reported by institution, keyed by UNITID, for institutions using semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4 or another predominantly academic credit-hour calendar. The record separates full-time undergraduate and graduate tuition and required fees, part-time undergraduate and graduate per-credit-hour charges, specified doctoral-professional programs, and the published attendance price for full-time first-time undergraduates, including tuition and fees, books, room and board, and other expenses.

Listed branch-campus location records contain the branch name, address, contact URLs, derived institutional classifications and award levels, keyed to the reporting main-campus UNITID and branch-location record. This is an optional, noncomprehensive College Navigator listing rather than a census of Title IV branches; cost-of-attendance fields are available only for listed branches enrolling full-time first-time undergraduates.

Vocational-program student charges are reported in one institution record keyed by UNITID for institutions using clock hours or primarily occupational credit-hour programs. Values cover the number of programs, the largest program’s attendance price, and tuition and books-and-supplies charges for up to five additional programs, with charges measured over the full program length rather than an academic year.
Institution mission information holds the mission statement or its web address for one institution, keyed by UNITID.

Award and enrollment outcomes for eight cohorts of degree- and certificate-seeking undergraduates entering degree-granting institutions from July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014. The cohorts are defined by first-time status, attendance intensity (full-time or part-time), and Pell-recipient status; each institution reports every entering student in one subcohort. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID and OMCHRT and include revised cohort size plus counts and percentages completing or still enrolled at four-, six-, and eight-year checkpoints: August 31, 2017, August 31, 2019, and August 31, 2021.

Student financial aid counts and dollar amounts broken down by undergraduate population, aid source, and aid type. The row grain is institution × student population (full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates or all undergraduates) × aid source/type, with total and average aid amounts; the detailed source categories apply to the first-time cohort, while the all-undergraduate population has totals for grants, Pell grants, and federal loans.

Average net price and its underlying financial-aid amounts for two groups of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates: those receiving grant or scholarship aid and those receiving Title IV federal aid. The row grain is institution × aid-recipient group; at public institutions, both groups are restricted to students paying in-district or in-state tuition, and the table is for degree-granting institutions.

Military, servicemember, and veteran benefit recipients and total benefit dollars broken down by student level and benefit type. The row grain is institution × student level (undergraduate or graduate) × benefit type, including Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits and Department of Defense Tuition Assistance; this collection is reported only in odd-numbered years, so 2021 (odd) has data.
